elevation.order: row-major, rows south to north, cell centres at e0 + (i + 0.5)·cell

current.meaning: Ebb direction; magnitude relative to the mean speed across the entrance (castle to castle)

town.order: row-major, rows south to north, cell centres at e0 + (i + 0.5)·cell
town.meaning: Ground (m ODN) over Dartmouth and Kingswear for the picture: the same LIDAR DTM at 4 m (the physics uses the 8 m grid)

waterMask.order: image rows north to south, cell centres at e0 + (i + 0.5)·cell
waterMask.encoding: signed distance (m) to the tidal water outline (shoreline layer) = (v - 128) / 2, > 0 in the water, clamped to about ±64 m
waterMask.meaning: Where the picture may draw the water surface: tidal water and the bank next to it, not low ground inland

layers.label: Terrain (land)
layers.source: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 2 m via Tilezen terrain tiles (AWS Open Data), z15, resampled to 8 m
layers.licence: Open Government Licence v3 (© Environment Agency copyright and/or database right 2015. All rights reserved.)
notes: Tile sources (tile counts): {'uk_lidar': 150, 'eudem': 56, 'srtm': 39, 'gmted': 45, 'etopo1': 43}. Where LIDAR coverage ends (offshore), tiles blend EU-DEM, SRTM, GMTED and ETOPO1.
Over Dartmouth and Kingswear the picture uses the same LIDAR at 4 m (town.i16z); the physics keeps the 8 m grid.

layers.label: Drying areas (mud, sand, rock)
layers.source: Same LIDAR DTM: ground above the water surface at the time of the survey, inside the tidal water mask
notes: 17943 cells of 8 m. Survey date and tide not known: the lower limit is the survey water level, about +0.4 m above chart datum.

layers.label: Water depth below the low-water line
layers.source: Estimate: depth grows with distance from the low-water edge (9 m cap in the harbour, rising seaward)
notes: No legally usable survey is available (Admiralty charts are UKHO copyright). Do not use for navigation.
Grounding in the app uses this depth: it is right near the shore (LIDAR) and only indicative mid-channel.

layers.label: Shoreline and tidal water
layers.source: OpenStreetMap coastline and riverbank polygons via Overture Maps 2026-10-21.0
layers.licence: ODbL 1.0 (© OpenStreetMap contributors, via Overture Maps Foundation)
notes: OSM positional accuracy not independently verified; the visible shoreline comes from the LIDAR terrain at the current tide.

layers.label: Terrain colour
layers.source: Copernicus Sentinel-2 L2A true colour, scene S2C_30UVA_20250712_0_L2A (12 Jul 2025), 10 m
layers.licence: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2025 (free and open)
notes: 10 m pixels: fields, woods and towns are recognisable; individual buildings are not.

layers.label: Buildings
layers.source: OpenStreetMap and Microsoft ML building footprints via Overture Maps 2026-10-21.0
layers.licence: ODbL 1.0 (© OpenStreetMap contributors, via Overture Maps Foundation); Microsoft ML Buildings ODbL
notes: 5404 footprints. Heights: 2041 from the data (Microsoft ML estimates or OSM), 392 from floor counts, 2971 estimated by building type (E).

Bases on the LIDAR ground (about 3 m in the towns). Roofs: OSM roof:shape where tagged; otherwise inferred (E) - terraces (shared party walls) gabled along the street, detached houses hipped or gabled, large and utility buildings flat ({'f': 626, 'g': 3246, 'h': 1532}; 1050 with party walls). Measured roof shapes need the Environment Agency LIDAR surface model (environment.data.gov.uk, not reachable from the build environment).

layers.label: Landmarks
layers.source: OSM names and footprints via Overture Maps 2026-10-21.0
layers.licence: ODbL 1.0 (© OpenStreetMap contributors, via Overture Maps Foundation)
notes: Shown as their real footprints with labels; churches roofed as gables along their length and castles flat (E). No invented towers or battlements.

layers.label: Piers, jetties and pontoons
layers.licence: ODbL 1.0 (© OpenStreetMap contributors, via Overture Maps Foundation)
notes: 92 features. Widths of line features and deck heights are estimates (E). Pontoons are assumed floating when tagged so or named 'Pontoon'.

layers.label: Mooring areas (trots)
layers.source: OpenStreetMap water polygons (Kingswear, Noss and Distins Trots; DHNA anchorage) via Overture Maps 2026-10-21.0
layers.licence: ODbL 1.0 (© OpenStreetMap contributors, via Overture Maps Foundation)
notes: 4 areas.

layers.label: Individual moorings and moored boats
layers.source: Generated: rows 22 m apart, buoys 16 m apart inside the mooring areas; boat types random (seeded)
notes: 443 moorings. Positions are illustrative: individual buoy positions are not established (N). They are not obstacles in the physics yet.

layers.label: Ferries
layers.source: Routes: OpenStreetMap ferry routes via Overture Maps 2026-10-21.0 (S). Timetables and vessel sizes: estimates (E)
layers.licence: ODbL 1.0 (© OpenStreetMap contributors, via Overture Maps Foundation)
notes: 9 route segments. Animation only: not obstacles in the physics yet. Lower and Higher Ferries are shown as restricted in their ability to manoeuvre (DHNA sailing directions, S(p)).

layers.label: Railway and Kingswear station
layers.source: OpenStreetMap railway lines, platform and station via Overture Maps 2026-10-21.0
layers.licence: ODbL 1.0 (© OpenStreetMap contributors, via Overture Maps Foundation)
notes: Track level follows the LIDAR ground; the tunnel is inferred from the ground rising far above the line (E).
Trains and their times: see the timetable notes in the app (docs/SOURCES.md).

layers.label: Marina berths and berthed boats
layers.source: Laid out in the app on OSM's pontoons (src/sim/env/marinas.ts): finger berths in the marinas, alongside on Dart Harbour's and the visitors' pontoons
notes: Berth spacing, boat sizes, how many berths are let by season and the marinas' daily movements are estimates (E). Published counts: Darthaven over 270 berths, Noss on Dart 155–232 (SOURCES.md F12, F13).
Berthed boats and pontoons are not obstacles in the physics yet.

layers.label: Steam trains
layers.source: The Dartmouth Steam Railway's published timetable for 25 Oct 2026 (Paignton 10:30, 12:00, 14:00, 15:30; Kingswear 11:10, 12:40, 14:40, 16:10; 30-minute journey), used for every day of the season
notes: Running days, the train's make-up and engine, speeds and the run-round at Kingswear are estimates (E). Visual only.

layers.label: Navigation marks
layers.source: Only marks with a stated position are placed (Castle Ledge buoy, visitmyharbour)
notes: Not placed (position not established): Checkstone and Homestone buoys, Kingswear light, RDYC racing marks.

layers.label: Tidal stream pattern
layers.source: Tidal-prism continuity on the provisional depths (potential flow), scaled to the entrance stream from the tide timing
notes: Not measured current data. The pattern depends on the provisional depths. Offshore (Start Bay) streams are not modelled.
